title: Indian Architecture as Tourist Attractions
meta: Lesson practice set · Question types of the April 2026 NIOS paper
instructions: Practice set for this lesson in the question types of the April 2026 paper.
Where a question has OR, answer either one.
Questions from previous NIOS papers show the exam they appeared in.

sections.title: Objective type questions: each has two parts of 1 mark (fill in the blanks, true/false, match the columns or one word).

questions.q: Fill in the blanks. (a) The Buddha's burial mounds built at Lumbini, Gaya, Sarnath and Kushinagar are called ________. (b) The Gateway of India in Mumbai was completed in ________ in the Indo-Saracenic style.

Fill in the blanks. (a) A very exciting place for tourists to visit are the sites of the ________ valley civilization. (b) The stupas of Sanchi and Sarnath are symbols of the achievement of ________ architecture.

Fill in the blanks. (a) During Ashoka's reign many monolithic stone pillars were erected on which teachings of ________ were inscribed. (b) The Lion Capital of the Sarnath Pillar has been adopted as the ________ of the Indian Republic.
True or False. (a) The Vedic Aryans built grand stone palaces that survive today. (b) Harappan cities followed a grid layout with roads cutting each other at right angles.
questions.answer: (a) False: they used wood, bamboo and reeds, so no Vedic structure survives. (b) True.

questions.q: Match Column A with Column B. A: (a) Dravida style (b) Nagara style. B: (i) Shikhara (spiral roof), garbhagriha and mandap (ii) Vimana, high walls and gopuram (iii) Domes and minarets.
Fill in the blanks. (a) The Kandariya Mahadev temple is at ________. (b) Brihadeshwara temple at Tanjore was built by the ________.
True or False. (a) The Taj Mahal is the tomb of Mumtaz Mahal built by Shah Jahan. (b) Humayun's Tomb was built of white marble.
questions.answer: (a) True. (b) False: it was built in red stone.

questions.q: Fill in the blanks. (a) The first free-standing Hindu temples were built in the ________ period. (b) The Rashtrapati Bhavan was designed by ________.
One word answers. (a) Which Gujarat site shows a Harappan dockyard? (b) Which city in Odisha has the Lingaraja and Mukteshwara temples?
True or False. (a) There were 2,837 towns in India in 1594 (Abul Fazl). (b) Delhi became the capital of British India in 1931.
questions.answer: (a) True. (b) False: in 1911 (New Delhi was completed by 1932).

sections.title: Very short answer questions. Answer in 30–50 words.

questions.q: Explain any two characteristics of rock-cut temples.
questions.answer: They were cut out of the rock, as at Karle, Ellora's Kailash temple and Mahabalipuram's rathas, and the stability of rock attracted patrons. They were decorated with beautiful sculptures.

questions.q: Explain the systematic evolution of Indian architecture in two points.
questions.answer: Indian architecture grew from Harappan town planning through Buddhist, Mauryan and Gupta temples to medieval Indo-Islamic styles. It was shaped by dynasties, regions and external influences, ending in colonial and modern styles.

questions.q: Describe the fire altars, the most important feature of Vedic architecture.
questions.answer: The Vedic Aryans built courtyards and mandaps with altars for worship of fire. Fire altars remain important in Hindu homes and marriages, but no Vedic structure survives because wood was used.

or.q: Describe two main characteristics of the beautiful temples of Odisha.
or.answer: They follow the Nagara style with shikharas, a garbhagriha and a mandap. Examples are the Lingaraja, Mukteshwara and Jagannath temples and the Konark Sun Temple, a twelve-wheeled chariot.

questions.q: Describe the town planning of the Harappan cities in two points.
questions.answer: Cities were built on a grid pattern with roads that cut each other at right angles. They had a citadel on high ground, an advanced drainage system and houses of well-baked bricks.

questions.q: Mention any two features of Mauryan architecture.
questions.answer: Highly polished monolithic stone pillars with animal capitals carried Ashoka's teachings. Stupas such as those at Sanchi and Sarnath show Mauryan skill.

questions.q: What is the Dravida style of architecture?
questions.answer: It is the South Indian temple style developed by the Cholas with a vimana or shikhara, high walls and a gateway topped with a gopuram.

questions.q: What is pietra dura?
questions.answer: It is decorative inlay work in stones, used in the Mughal buildings of Shah Jahan, such as the Taj Mahal.

questions.q: Name the two Buddhist architectural forms and state their use.
questions.answer: A stupa is a mound built over Buddha's relics and at sites of his life events. A vihara is a monastery and a chaitya is a congregational hall for preaching and teaching.

questions.q: Why is Howrah Bridge a symbol of Kolkata? Give two points.
questions.answer: It crosses the Hooghly river and connects Howrah to Kolkata. It stands on two 270 ft pillars and was built without nuts and bolts, being probably the busiest bridge in the world.

sections.title: Short answer questions. Answer in 50–80 words.

questions.q: Analyse the impacts of the British on Indian architecture in three points.
questions.answer: (i) Greek and Roman colonnaded buildings such as Parliament House and Connaught Place were built. (ii) Gothic and Indo-Saracenic buildings appeared, such as St Paul's Cathedral, Victoria Terminus and the Gateway of India, along with Lutyens's Rashtrapati Bhavan combining jaali and canopies. (iii) New cities, ports, railway terminals, hill stations, Civil Lines and cantonments were planned.

questions.q: Explain any three characteristics of burial mounds (stupas).
questions.answer: (i) Stupas were huge mud mounds enclosed in burnt bricks, built where Buddha's remains were kept. (ii) They stand at his birthplace Lumbini, Gaya, Sarnath and Kushinagar. (iii) Viharas and chaityas grew around them and they became tourist landmarks.

questions.q: Explain the contribution of the Gupta, Pallava and Chola rulers to temple architecture (three points).
questions.answer: (i) The Guptas began free-standing temples with a garbhagriha (Deogarh, Bhitargaon). (ii) The Pallavas built the Shore temple, rathas and Kanchipuram temples. (iii) The Cholas built the Brihadeshwara temple and developed the Dravida style with vimana and gopuram.

questions.q: Explain the Mughal style of architecture (three points).
questions.answer: (i) Humayun's Tomb, Agra and Fatehpur Sikri with the Buland Darwaza show a synthesis of Persian and Indian elements. (ii) Shah Jahan used marble and pietra dura in the Red Fort, Jama Masjid and the Taj Mahal. (iii) Gardens around tombs, such as Shalimar, were a unique development.

questions.q: Describe the architecture of the Delhi Sultanate (three points).
questions.answer: (i) Turks brought domes, arches and minarets and used local craftsmen, blending Islamic and Indian styles. (ii) Qutub Minar (70 m), Quwwat-ul-Islam mosque and Alai Darwaza are examples. (iii) Tughlaq buildings had massive, strong walls because of Mongol threats.

sections.title: Long answer questions. Answer in 80–120 words.

questions.q: Explain the architectural styles from the Harappan period to the Gupta period in six points.
questions.answer: (i) Harappan cities had grid planning, drains, public baths and brick houses. (ii) The Vedic period used wood and fire altars. (iii) Buddhist and Jain stupas, viharas and chaityas appeared. (iv) Mauryan polished pillars and the Sanchi and Sarnath stupas, with the lion capital as national emblem. (v) Cave architecture at Ajanta, Ellora and Udaygiri, and rock-cut temples at Karle. (vi) Gupta period began free-standing temples at Deogarh and Bhitargaon.

questions.q: Describe the contribution of Buddhism and Jainism to Indian architecture and the regional temple styles, in six points.
questions.answer: (i) Buddhists built stupas at Lumbini, Gaya, Sarnath and Kushinagar. (ii) Viharas and chaityas became centres of teaching. (iii) Caves of Ajanta and Ellora hold Buddhist halls. (iv) Dilwara Jain temples at Mount Abu are built in white marble. (v) The Dravida style of the South has vimana and gopuram. (vi) The Nagara style of the North and East has shikhara, garbhagriha and mandap (Konark, Khajuraho).

questions.q: The architecture of the Mughal period was a synthesis of Indian, Persian and Central Asian styles. Explain in six points.
questions.answer: (i) Humayun's Tomb in red stone with a garden is a precursor of the Taj. (ii) Akbar built the forts at Agra and Fatehpur Sikri. (iii) The Buland Darwaza (41 m) reflects Mughal grandeur. (iv) Jahangir built Akbar's mausoleum and the marble tomb of Itimad-ud-daula. (v) Shah Jahan used marble and pietra dura in the Red Fort, Jama Masjid and the Taj Mahal. (vi) Living beings were carved in brackets and gardens such as Shalimar were laid.
